task_name: `App.tsx`: un solo estado de carga y un despacho exhaustivo

rubric.result: The objective promises four things and all four are in the diff. (1) 'una sola pieza de estado por carga': the pair `useState<Summary|null>` + `useState<ApiErrorCode|null>` is replaced by a single `const [load, setLoad] = useState<SummaryLoad>({ status: 'loading' })` (App.tsx:25), and every branch of both effects now writes that one piece (`setLoad({status:'failed'|'loaded'|'loading'})`, lines 46, 54, 64, 67). (2) 'pide la pantalla a ScreenChoice': `const { screen } = ScreenChoice.of({ repos, repoId, load })` (App.tsx:72). (3) 'despacha sobre el vocabulario sin rama por defecto': `screenBody` (App.tsx:110-139) is a `switch` over `screen.kind` with one `return` per member of the five-member `Screen` and no `default`, with `ReactElement` declared as its return type. (4) 'la carpeta sin .git enseña su estado diseñado con la lista de clones': case `not-a-git-repo` renders `<Screens.NotAGitRepo repoId clones onRepo>` (App.tsx:115), which draws the headline `NOT_A_GIT_REPO_HEADLINE` and one button per detected clone (Screens.tsx:43-66), and the new test pins exactly that.

The TDD line names `test('a folder without .git shows the designed screen with the list of clones')` and fixes the assertion: the double answers `not-a-git-repo` to the summary, and the screen brings at once the headline `Esa carpeta no es un repositorio git` and a button with the name of the clone in the list, so the generic failure copy in its place would fail it. The test in the diff (App.test.tsx:143-155) is that test: input is `stubApiWithoutSummary({ kind: 'failed', code: 'not-a-git-repo' })`, which answers the clone list for `/api/repos` and the error envelope `{error:{code:'not-a-git-repo'}}` for the summary; it asserts `await screen.findByText('Esa carpeta no es un repositorio git')`, then `screen.getByRole('button', { name: /alpha-clone/ }).textContent` equals `'alpha-clone · /git/alpha'` (the clone of the list, by the name the header uses), and finally that `queryByText(/No se ha podido cargar la información/)` is null — which is the 'with the generic code in its place the test falls' half made explicit. Both literals come from production (`format.ts:163`, `Screens.tsx:46,60`), so the assertion is over the real copy, not over a value the test defined.

The brief carries no `Contract (path):` block; it carries two `Current state` blocks and one `Call site` block, and I measured against those. Both `Current state` lines are gone: `{error !== null &&

…}` and `{error === null && summary === null &&

Cargando…

}` are removed, and the alert copy now lives in `Screens.Failed`; the `App.test.tsx` lines 129-132 wait on `Cargando…` is gone too. The prose contract holds name by name: `screenBody` is a module-level function of `App.tsx` (like the two it already had), a `switch` over `screen.kind`, one `return` per member, no default branch, declared `: ReactElement`; `blocks` returns today's grid; the other four return their `Screens` component; `setError` and `repoNameOf` both disappear and `HeatBlock` gets `repoName={screen.repoName}` from the `blocks` member. Two divergences from the `Call site` block, and neither is satisfiable inside this task, so I record them rather than count them. (i) The block writes `const { screen, history, snapshot } = ScreenChoice.of(...)` and `
`; the diff writes `const { screen } = …` and `meta={load.status === 'loaded' ? load.summary.meta : null}`. `HeaderProps` (Header.tsx:5-14) declares `meta: SummaryMeta | null` and declares neither `history` nor `snapshot`, and `Header.tsx` is not in this task's `**Files:**` (it is rewired in task 6): passing those two props is a JSX excess-property type error, and destructuring them unused is an `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` error, so either form contradicts this same task's `**Verification:**` (`npm run build && npm run lint # expected: exit 0`). (ii) The block writes `screenBody(screen)` and the prose types it `screenBody(screen: Screen): ReactElement`; the diff adds a second typed parameter `Shell` (`repoId`, `window`, `onRepo`). No member of `Screen` (screen.ts:13-18) carries `repoId`+`window` — which `TrendPanel` and `HeatBlock` need — nor `onRepo`, which the clone buttons need, and `screen.ts` is not in `**Files:**` either. The declared return type, which is what the closed decision makes the exhaustiveness gate, is untouched.

Row by row over the rows this diff bears on. 'Qué sustituye al par summary/error': implemented exactly — one `load: SummaryLoad` of three members (`loading`, `loaded`, `failed`), App.tsx:25. 'Cómo se despacha en TSX sin rama por defecto': implemented — `function screenBody(screen: Screen, shell: Shell): ReactElement` with the return type declared, App.tsx:110. 'Forma de esa decisión' (five-member closed vocabulary, exhaustive dispatch, no default): implemented — five `case`s, no `default`. 'Quién decide el nombre del repo seleccionado': implemented — `repoNameOf` is deleted from `App.tsx` and the name is read off the `blocks` member (`repoName={screen.repoName}`, App.tsx:132). 'Cómo se exponen los de un módulo .tsx que ya estaba': `App.tsx` keeps its default export. 'Dónde vive el castellano nuevo': the diff adds no Spanish copy to `App.tsx`; the new tests assert literals produced by `format.ts` (`analysingHeadline`, `NOT_A_GIT_REPO_HEADLINE`, `NO_COMMITS_HEADLINE`, `NO_COMMITS_FOOTNOTE`). Rows the diff does not touch (dónde vive la decisión, quién decide si la foto está caducada, ventana de la llamada a la acción, módulos .tsx nuevos, referencia visual) are task 1-4 and task 6-7 subjects. One row lands half-way and it is the same forced deviation as item 3(i): 'De dónde sale la frescura de la foto — del Clone que devuelve GET /repos, nunca de summary.meta'. The header still receives `meta` derived from `load.summary.meta`, because the vehicle the plan chose for that row is the `snapshot` prop and `HeaderProps` does not declare it until task 6, which this task may not touch. The diff does not reopen the decision or implement a competing one — `ScreenChoice.snapshotOf` already reads it from the `Clone` (screen.ts:108-116) — it just cannot wire it yet, so I record it instead of counting it.

Exemplars: `web/src/App.test.tsx` is the named exemplar for the fetch double and the new `stubApiWithoutSummary` follows its idiom (`vi.stubGlobal('fetch', …)`, `as unknown as Response`, the shared `CLONES` constant, `windowOf` reused rather than re-derived); `web/src/Heat.tsx`'s way of drawing states is respected in that all copy comes from `format.ts` through `Screens`. AGENTS.md rules that bear on this diff all hold: strict TypeScript and ESM, tests beside the code, every new identifier in English (`SummaryLoad`, `UnlandedSummary`, `stubApiWithoutSummary`, `Shell`, `screenBody`) with the visible Spanish left in `format.ts`, `web/` importing nothing from `server/`, and no author name or email in the DOM (the pre-existing leak test still passes). No skill is named in §3, so none was loaded. `conventions/defects.md`, its four rules, one verdict each: (1) closed vocabulary — conforming, and it is the point of the task: the loose pair is replaced by the three-member `SummaryLoad`, the dispatch over `Screen` has five cases and no catch-all, and even the new test helper classifies with a closed `UnlandedSummary = {kind:'failed';code} | {kind:'pending'}` switched exhaustively (App.test.tsx:114, 130-139); (2) raw map as the return value of logic — no subject: nothing in the diff returns or receives an untyped map; `Shell` (App.tsx:99-103) is a declared interface of three named fields read by field access, and `ScreenChoice.of` returns the typed `Dashboard`; (3) two fields that have to agree — the diff removes one instead of adding one (`summary`/`error` are gone); the only absence left is the `SummaryMeta | null` the pre-existing `HeaderProps` declares, which is Header's own contract and task 6's subject, not a pair introduced here; (4) an error named for where it happens — no subject: the diff adds no error type and leaves `codeOf` untouched. `conventions/style.md`: `App.tsx` and `App.test.tsx` are pre-existing modules that already carry docstrings and module-level functions, so the new docstrings on `Shell`/`screenBody`/`stubApiWithoutSummary` and `screenBody` living at module level follow the host's style — declared debt, and the plan's closed decision says the same. `conventions/architecture.md` applies to new modules and this diff creates none. `conventions/decisions.md`: the screen decision is written once, in `screen.ts`; `App.tsx` no longer derives any screen or repo name of its own. No boundary or delivery-shape rule in either yardstick is contradicted: dependencies still arrive as props/parameters (`onRepo` is injected into `Screens.NotAGitRepo`), and the transitional `meta` prop is the shape the plan itself chose for reaching task 6.

The `-` lines in `App.test.tsx` touch exactly the two tests the brief names under `**Tests:**` as 'Modificados en su aserción, con el mismo nombre'. In `without dates the header shows neither` the removed `await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByText('Cargando…')).toBeNull())` is replaced by `await screen.findByText('Pulso')` + `getByText('/git/alpha')` + `queryByText('Analizando alpha-clone…')).toBeNull()`: the same two absences are still asserted and the anchor is now positive, so the test ends up stricter, not weaker. In `changing the window asks the API for that window` the removed `expect(urls.at(-1)).toContain('window=12m')` and `toContain('window=all')` are replaced by `expect(urls.filter((url) => url.includes('/summary?')).map(windowOf)).toEqual(['12m', 'all'])`, an exact sequence over the summary requests only — again stricter, and it removes the chance that a heat URL is what makes it pass. The brief's literal instruction ('esa espera pasa a mirar el titular nuevo') is honoured by the `queryByText('Analizando alpha-clone…')` assertion while a bare wait on that headline would have gone green on the first tick (before the clone list lands the headline reads `Analizando …`), so the deviation is a strengthening the brief's own sentence asks for. No other pre-existing assertion, case or test is removed or relaxed.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code, not by scaffolding. The dispatch that turns state into a screen is `screenBody` in `App.tsx` (production, this diff) over `ScreenChoice.of` and `Screens` (production, committed in tasks 1-4); every literal the three new tests assert is produced by `format.ts` (`Analizando ${repoName}…`, `Esa carpeta no es un repositorio git`, `Repositorio sin commits`, `Cuando entre el primer commit, esta pantalla se llena sola.`) and rendered by `Screens.tsx`, and the clone button's `'alpha-clone · /git/alpha'` is composed in `Screens.NotAGitRepo`, not in the test. The only doubles are the `fetch` stubs, which stand in for the network and decide nothing about which screen is drawn: revert `App.tsx` in this diff and the three new tests fail, since the old body renders `

Cargando…

` or the generic alert.

Everything written inside the two declared files answers a sentence of the task. In `App.tsx`: the single `load` state and its four writes (objective), `ScreenChoice.of` (objective), `screenBody` with its `switch` (objective and the prose contract), `interface Shell` (the parameters `blocks` and `not-a-git-repo` need and `Screen` does not carry), the `ReactElement` type import, the removal of `repoNameOf` and of the `Summary` type import (the contract says `repoNameOf` disappears). In `App.test.tsx`: the three new tests the `**Tests:**` line names one by one, the `stubApiWithoutSummary`/`UnlandedSummary` helper they need (the existing `stubApi` always lands a payload, so neither the failed nor the pending case is reachable through it), the `ApiErrorCode` type import it uses, and the two modified assertions the same line authorises. Nothing named in `### Out of scope` appears: no `Traer cambios` button, no step-by-step progress in the loading screen (the analysing screen is a single indeterminate bar), no `Elegir otra carpeta…` button in the not-a-git-repo screen, no server change, no demo-state chips. No refactor, rename or adjacent fix rides along. The one thing that goes slightly beyond the letter of the brief is how far the window assertion was strengthened (exact sequence, summary URLs only) inside a test the brief explicitly authorises modifying — worth noting, not code the task did not ask for.

Three new tests, and the three blocking properties hold for each. Deterministic: none reads the real clock or today's date in an assertion (the only date-shaped literals are the ISO strings the double answers with), none touches the network (`fetch` is stubbed) or the filesystem, none uses randomness or a sleep — the analysing case pins the in-flight screen with a promise that never settles (`return new Promise<Response>(() => undefined)`) precisely so no timer decides the outcome, and the waits are `findByText`/`waitFor` on the DOM. Isolated: each test installs its own `fetch` stub, `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in the setup file undoes it after each test, the only shared state is the frozen `CLONES`/`HEAT_TREE` constants which nothing mutates, and none of the three needs a predecessor or leaves anything behind — they were inserted at the top of the file and the tests after them still pass. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on rendered production output (copy from `format.ts` drawn by `Screens.tsx`, the `progressbar` role of the real progress bar, the composed button text), and each of the three would fail with this diff's `App.tsx` reverted. No finer remark to report, so the TDD skill was not needed as a yardstick here.
